cases.excerpt: The present case-control study (103 cases and 200 controls) was a hospital-based investigation conducted in three referral hospitals in Tehran, Iran.

effect_size.excerpt: After adjusting confounding factors, it was observed that the odds of bladder cancer were significantly lower in the second and last tertiles (T) of total peptide intake from dairy products compared to the first tertile (T<sub>2</sub>: odds ratio (OR) = 0.285; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.116-0.699, T<sub>3</sub>: OR = 0.130; 95% CI: 0.032-0.527). Additionally, in the adjusted model, a significant inverse association was found between other dairy-derived peptides and the odds of bladder cancer.
